qualifier: Yes, Fort Lauderdale requires a permit from its Development Services Department for seawalls. A substantial repair (more than 50% of the shoreline length or more than 50% of replacement cost) must bring the wall up to the city's tidal flood barrier height. Broward County also requires its own Environmental Resource License, usually a quick general license for a repair in the same place.
detail_rows: City :: Permit from the Development Services Department before building mooring structures; 'mooring structure' includes a seawall - Code Sec. 8-91(a)(2), (b). Seawall permits need a current signed and sealed survey and Zoning Affidavit - Permitting Services page. Substantial repair or rehabilitation (work along more than 50% of the shoreline length or over 50% of replacement cost) must meet the tidal flood barrier elevation (5.0 ft NAVD88; 4.0 ft for applications before 1 Jan 2035) - ULDR Sec. 47-19.13 | Broward County :: Work in regulated waters needs a county Environmental Resource License (ERL) - Broward County Code Sec. 27-333(a)(1). Repair, maintenance or restoration of an existing functional seawall no more than 1 ft waterward of its authorized location (or a new wall within 1 ft of the old wet face with the old wall left in place) qualifies for a general license - Sec. 27-336(a)(1)b.; so do refacing, crack filling, seepage holes and other minor repairs (Sec. 27-336(a)(1)n.) and raising the cap in the same footprint (Sec. 27-336(a)(1)o.).
